Comments: No credible, primary evidence captured for an integrated online tax portal with digital payment (end-to-end) accessible via a citable government source in the materials gathered; searched for impots.cm/DGI documentation and reputable confirmations but did not retrieve an accessible primary reference page.

revision_notes: Fetched and confirmed DGI's official e-services portal (impots.cm, teledeclaration-dgi.cm, otp.dgi.cm) offering online tax filing and e-payment, integrated with the Treasury's Tresor Pay platform (dgi.tresorpublic.cm) supporting MTN MoMo, Orange Money (including USSD), Campost, bank transfer and card. revised_comments: Cameroon's Directorate General of Taxation (DGI) operates an official online tax portal (impots.cm, teledeclaration-dgi.cm, otp.dgi.cm) enabling taxpayers to file returns and pay tax notices electronically. Payment is integrated with the Treasury's Tresor Pay platform (dgi.tresorpublic.cm), which accepts MTN Mobile Money, Orange Money (including via USSD codes), Campost, bank transfer and Visa card. Decree No. 2022/8001 establishes the legal framework for electronic payment of taxes, customs duties and other state revenue. As of May 2026 the service is in active use by taxpayers in Yaoundé's local tax centres (CFLP), with plans to extend nationally.

Comments: No credible, citable evidence found in the collected sources for a broad, official P2G capability for paying government fees/taxes at scale (beyond limited mentions without accessible primary documentation); searched for DGI/impots.cm mobile money payment documentation and reputable confirmations but did not retrieve a usable primary source page.

revision_notes: Decree No. 2022/8001 legally authorises electronic P2G payments (taxes, customs, fees, fines and other state dues) via mobile money, online payment and payment terminals. The Treasury's Tresor Pay platform (tresorpublic.cm) implements this for non-tax revenue across ministries, and a May 2025 prime ministerial order made its use mandatory for several government departments within three months. DGI tax payment via Tresor Pay/mobile money is confirmed operational (May 2026). Score upgraded from 0/Unknown to 3/Yes-Active Use given the clear legal basis and confirmed live, mandated use.
revised_comments: Citizens can pay a broad range of government charges — taxes, customs duties, fees and non-tax revenues — electronically via the Treasury's Tresor Pay platform and the DGI's online/mobile money channels (MTN MoMo, Orange Money, Campost, bank transfer, card). Decree No. 2022/8001 provides the legal basis for electronic P2G payments to the State and public entities. A May 2025 prime ministerial order made Tresor Pay mandatory for several government departments collecting non-tax revenue, and by 2026 tax payment via mobile money and Tresor Pay is in active use in Yaoundé's tax centres, indicating genuine adoption rather than a merely notional capability.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No credible evidence found of a mandatory data-breach notification requirement applicable to payment providers in Cameroon in the sources reviewed (searched for ‘Cameroon data breach notification law payments’ and reviewed summaries of the cybersecurity framework).
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 (Personal Data Protection Law) requires data controllers and processors — a category that includes payment service providers — to notify the Personal Data Protection Authority and affected data subjects immediately upon becoming aware of any breach, with joint and several liability for unlawful disclosure. An 18-month compliance grace period runs to 23 June 2026. The requirement is general rather than payment-specific, but clearly covers payment transaction data as personal data. Score upgraded from 0/Unknown to 3/Mandatory.
revised_comments: Cameroon's Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection imposes a mandatory breach-notification duty on data controllers and processors, who must immediately inform both the newly created Personal Data Protection Authority and affected data subjects of any breach, regardless of severity. Controllers and processors are jointly and severally liable for unlawful disclosure of data, which extends to payment transaction data held by payment service providers. Enforcement is subject to an 18-month compliance grace period ending 23 June 2026.

revision_notes: Re-fetched the AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 case study, which confirms GIMACPAY operates on a cost-recovery fee-band basis but does not evidence full public rulebook access. Checked GIMAC's own website (gimac-afr.com), which publicly hosts downloadable 'Modalités d'adhésion' (membership/participation terms) documents for members and payment aggregators, describing onboarding requirements (KYC/AML compliance, technical, financial and commercial conditions) with no login required. This shows partial public disclosure of participation rules rather than complete confidentiality, but the full technical rulebook and pricing schedule are not confirmed public. The originally cited IMF ROSC source (dated 2000) describes a pre-GIMACPAY payment system and is no longer relevant. Revised from 1/No-Confidential to 2/Partial-On Request.
revised_comments: GIMAC, the regional operator of the GIMACPAY instant payment scheme for CEMAC (including Cameroon), publishes membership and participation requirements ('Modalités d'adhésion') openly on its website for both direct participants and payment aggregators, covering governance, technical, compliance (KYC/AML) and commercial conditions for joining the scheme. The full technical rulebook, detailed pricing structure and security standards are not confirmed to be published in full to the general public, indicating partial rather than complete transparency of scheme rules.

GIMAC, operator of the GIMACPAY instant payment scheme, separately undergoes independent PCI DSS security certification (renewed in early 2026 by assessor DATAPROTECT), with the certification renewal publicly announced. Together these constitute independent, publicly disclosed audits and security reviews of the payment system's financial and operational controls.

Definition: Whether refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, migrants, and stateless persons can legally access and open digital payment accounts, and practical barriers or enablers for these populations.
Comments: No credible evidence found in the gathered sources of specific provisions enabling refugee/migrant access to digital payment systems in Cameroon (e.g., simplified KYC for refugees for mobile money). Searched for ‘Cameroon refugee mobile money KYC’ and ‘Cameroon migrant access mobile money’ without finding a citable, authoritative policy/program reference.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The GSMA/UNHCR 'Displaced and Disconnected' country report confirms refugees and asylum seekers in Cameroon are issued UNHCR refugee ID cards (CIR) and asylum-seeker certificates that are legally recognised (per the Law of 27 July 2005) and accepted for SIM registration; CIRs are also accepted by some providers for mobile money account opening under BEAC's electronic money regulation (No. 01/11 CEMAC/UMAC/CM), with refugee mobile money penetration reported at 15.14% (World Bank Global Findex). However, the same source notes refugees often face difficulties with institutions unfamiliar with refugee documentation, sometimes requiring UNHCR intervention. A 2022 biometric ID pilot for CAR refugees explicitly aims to enable bank account access. Evidence supports upgrading from 0/Unknown to 2/Partial (legal pathway exists but with practical access barriers), not to 3/Yes given the documented friction.
revised_comments: Refugees and asylum seekers in Cameroon are issued UNHCR-recognised identity documents (refugee ID cards/CIR and asylum-seeker certificates) that are legally accepted for SIM card registration and, under BEAC's electronic money regulation, for opening mobile money accounts; a 2022 pilot also issues biometric ID cards to refugees explicitly to enable bank account access. In practice, however, some mobile money and banking providers are unfamiliar with refugee documentation and refuse registration, occasionally requiring UNHCR advocacy on behalf of affected individuals, so access remains partial rather than fully assured.
